chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa,man ibn 'Isa, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Suleym ibn Qays, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah has prohibited Paradise upon every immoral one, obscene one, little of shame, nor caring what he says nor what is said for him, for if you scrutinize him, you will not find him except as a strayed one or an associate of Satan.'

So it was said, 'O Rasool-Allah, and among the people are associates of Satan?' So Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Have you not read the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: and shares with them in wealth and the children?'

He (the narrator) said, 'And a man asked a Scholar, 'Is there among the people, the one who does not care what is said for him?' He said: 'The one who exposes the obscenities to the people and he knows that they would not be leaving him. So that is the one who does not care what he says and what is said regarding him'.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual signs of being an associate of Satan according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that obscene speech and modesty are not merely social graces but spiritual determinants of Paradise, linking the 'associate of Satan' (shirk al-shaytan) to a specific psychological state of indifference. The scholarly tradition interprets this indifference as a conscious choice to engage in mutual abuse despite knowing the consequences, thereby validating the Quranic reference to Satan's share in wealth and offspring as a metaphor for those who bear his mark. It serves as a practical guide for self-examination, urging believers to cultivate haya (modesty) as a shield against the devil's influence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Umar Bin Azina, from Aban Bin Abu Ayyash, from Suleym Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Prohibited the Paradise upon every immoral one, obscene one, little of shame, nor caring what he says nor what is said for him, If you inquire, you will not find him to be except as a strayed one or an associate of the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.

So it was said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww, and among the people are associates of Satanla?’ So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Have you not read the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [17:64] and shares with them in wealth and the children?’

He (the narrator) said, ‘And a man asked a Scholar<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there among the people, the one who does not care what is said for him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who exposes the obscenities to the people and he knows that they would not be leaving him. So that is the one who does not care what he says and what is said regarding him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Aban ibn abu ‘Ayyash from Sulaym ibn Qays from Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Allah has made paradise unlawful for every abusive, immoral, and (persons) lacking bashfulness who is not concerned about what he says or what is said to him. If (investigated) you find him to be an straying person or a partner of Satan.’

It was asked, O Messenger of Allah, ‘Does Satan become a partner of people?’ the Messenger of Allah said, ‘Have you not read the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘ . . . share them in their properties and children. . . .’ [17:64]

“The narrator has said that a man then asked a one learned in the law (the Imam), ‘Is there among the people anyone who is not concerned about what he says or what is said about him?’ The Imam said, ‘One who disturbs people and abuses them knowing that people do not leave him without a response, such a person is the one who is not concerned about what he says or what is said about him.’”
